facts.text: North Anson was named after British Admiral George Anson when Anson town incorporated in 1798, and it briefly split off in 1845 before rejoining in 1855.
Before Europeans arrived, North Anson lay within Abenaki territory, where the Norridgewock band lived along the Kennebec and Carrabassett rivers.
North Anson sits at the confluence of the Kennebec and Carrabassett rivers, a spot that shaped its early transport and hydrology.
North Anson’s economy once hinged on farming hay, potatoes, oats, and apples, plus sawmills, woolen factories, and tanneries from the 1800s to 1900s.
Pan Am Railways reopened a spur to North Anson in 2007, but service ended in 2013, and the line is now a planned rail trail.
